Need a later pass for pumps, valves, heat exchangers, sensors, leak detection, coolant chemistry, commissioning, and field-service bottlenecks; this pass primarily found public-market evidence for cooling systems, switchgear, and electrical installation components.

POWL should be tracked as an underfollowed electrical BOP candidate for AI data centers because its medium-voltage switchgear exposure and data-center backlog may make it a deployment bottleneck, but project lumpiness and end-market concentration must be checked.
MOD should be tracked as an underfollowed thermal BOP candidate because its data-center cooling growth is explicit in FY2026 filings and may benefit from AI rack-density and liquid-cooling adoption.
NVT should be tracked as a diversified electrification and enclosure supplier with plausible AI data-center BOP exposure across liquid cooling, power distribution, cable management, and bus systems.

The AI data-center power and thermal BOP node should be split in later layers into electrical distribution/switchgear, thermal/liquid cooling, electrical connection/enclosures/busway, and field execution/services because each has different evidence and bottleneck dynamics.

Need primary-source verification for additional small/mid-cap suppliers in pumps, valves, sensors, testing/certification, and field services; current pass found stronger evidence for switchgear, cooling, and electrical connection/protection than for pumps/valves/testing gates.

POWL should remain in the data-center power BOP universe as a direct switchgear/packaged-power candidate with a disclosed $400M-plus data-center order; later layers must test cyclicality, customer concentration and order lumpiness.

NVT is a large-cap but unusually relevant bridge between electrical protection, racks, PDUs and liquid cooling; keep as an underfollowed/reference hybrid rather than a pure small-cap discovery name.

IESC is a low-attention field-execution and electrical/technology infrastructure services candidate; data-center demand is explicitly cited, but later layers need segment-level quantification and backlog evidence.

Potential missing subnodes for later Layer 1B passes: transformer manufacturers, busway/raceway suppliers, generator/fuel systems, controls/sensors, valves/pumps, test/commissioning firms, and specialty distributors with data-center customer exposure.
